chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, by his chain, from the one who mentioned it, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man enters a city, he is a guest upon those in it from his brethren and the people of his religion, until he departs from them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hospitality for a traveler entering a new city?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the communal obligation of hospitality (diyafah) in Shia jurisprudence, framing the traveler not merely as a visitor but as a temporary member of the local religious community. It reflects the broader Islamic principle of social solidarity, where the host city assumes responsibility for the traveler's welfare until his departure, reinforcing the bonds of brotherhood (ukhuwwah) across geographical boundaries.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, by his chain, from the one who mentioned it, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When a man enters a city, so he is a guest upon the ones in it from his brethren, and the people of his Religion until he departs from them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘ Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar through the chain of his narrators from those whom he has mentioned from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “When a man enters a town he then is a guest of his brothers (in belief) who live there and the people of his religion until he leaves that town.”’
